name: Ruby on Rails Conventions
description: Rails — convention over configuration, fat models thin controllers, concerns, service objects, ActiveRecord
content:
# Ruby on Rails Conventions

- Follow convention over configuration — use Rails defaults for file structure, naming, and routing unless there is a clear reason not to
- Keep controllers thin — controllers handle HTTP concerns only (params, redirects, rendering). Move business logic to models or service objects
- Use concerns (`ActiveSupport::Concern`) to share behavior across models or controllers — keep each concern focused on one responsibility
- Extract complex business logic into service objects (plain Ruby classes in `app/services/`) — each service does one thing
- Use ActiveRecord scopes for reusable query logic — chain scopes for readable, composable queries
- Use strong parameters (`params.require().permit()`) in every controller — never pass unfiltered params to model methods
- Write database migrations that are reversible — always define both `up` and `down` or use reversible change methods
- Use background jobs (Sidekiq/ActiveJob) for slow operations — never make users wait for emails, API calls, or heavy processing
- Validate data at the model level with ActiveRecord validations — use custom validators for complex rules
- Use `has_many :through` for many-to-many relationships — avoid `has_and_belongs_to_many` as it lacks a join model for future flexibility
